title: Heat Pump Economics in Massachusetts
summary: A Massachusetts energy consultant compares heat pump running costs and emissions with gas, oil, propane and resistance heat using NEEP COP data and Worcester weather.

assertions.quote: they use electricity to pump heat from one location to the other
electric resistance is over four thousand dollars while air source heat pumps are listed at close to one thousand five hundred dollars
home heating oil we would see that it's always also going to be more expensive than a heat pump
right now when we are looking at this and looking at today's fuel prices natural gas is going to be the most affordable
as the temperature drops down to 17 degrees we'll see the coefficient of performance has dropped down to 2.64
how is that heat pump performing really between here and here where we do have the most amount of hours

verdicts.note: Bin-hour weather data show most heating hours fall at moderate temperatures, so seasonal COP sits closer to the mild-weather figure.
With a 10F changeover a heat pump meets 71% of the heating load in Duluth and 81% in Minneapolis, so most heating load falls at temperatures above 10F where the heat pump runs.

In Massachusetts/Rhode Island, very few winter hours fell below 0 F and the median winter hour was about 30 F (2015) or 38 F (2016), so most heating happens well above the cold extremes where efficiency is worst.
